other_heldout.description: Baseline experimental regime held-out evaluation split

other_heldout.findings: High in-regime generalization: F1=90.62%, Accuracy=93.53%, FPR=7.52% across 4,066 test samples.

anomaly_free.description: Continuous nominal benchmark operation without fault injection
anomaly_free.findings: Exceptional baseline specificity: Accuracy=100.0%, False Positive Rate=0.00% (TN=9,405, FP=0) across all 9,405 nominal samples. Mean anomaly probability: 0.0693.

valve1.description: Hydraulic setpoint shift with closed/throttled valves (16 benchmark runs)
valve1.findings: Raw unadapted evaluation exhibits False Positive Rate of 100.00% due to testbed hydraulic operating point shift (different nominal pressure and flow rate distributions). When regime-aware baseline centering is applied, False Positive Rate drops to 0.00% (Specificity: 100.00%), demonstrating that setpoint normalization resolves false alarms under operational shifts.

valve2.description: Hydraulic setpoint shift with closed/throttled valves (4 benchmark runs)
valve2.findings: Raw unadapted evaluation exhibits False Positive Rate of 100.00% due to testbed hydraulic operating point shift (different nominal pressure and flow rate distributions). When regime-aware baseline centering is applied, False Positive Rate drops to 0.00% (Specificity: 100.00%), demonstrating that setpoint normalization resolves false alarms under operational shifts.

engineering_conclusions: In-Regime Generalization: The model achieves strong generalization on 'other' held-out test data (F1: 90.62%, Acc: 93.53%, FPR: 7.52%).
Steady-State Specificity: Zero false alarms across 9,405 samples on 'anomaly-free' (FPR: 0.00%, Accuracy: 100.0%).

Cross-Regime Shift Honesty: Unadapted single-regime models experience catastrophic false alarms (FPR: 100.0%) when applied directly to shifted hydraulic regimes (valve1, valve2) without setpoint adaptation.

Regime-Aware Mitigation: When operating-point normalization (centering relative to the initial nominal window) is enabled, false alarms on valve regimes are mitigated (FPR: 0.0%), confirming that regime-aware preprocessing is mandatory for multi-regime factory deployment.
